args.text: I'd be upfront but constructive about it. I'd say something like, "I'm happy to take this on, but to be fair, I have some concerns about the deadline. Then I'd walk them through the main risks and suggest either a revised date or reducing the scope, so it's not just a complaint but a proposal.

conversation.title: Raising a missed deadline at the coffee machine
conversation.goal: Name the impact of a late handover, set a boundary, and agree a next step without blame.

turns.text: Ah, the coffee machine's eaten my euro again! You've a look about you, so what's on your mind?

Hi Declan, yeah, to be fair, it's a bit awkward. The figures from your team came in two days late, so we had to rush the whole report and I'd say the quality suffered. I don't want to make it a big deal, but could we agree on a firmer handover date next time?
Fair enough, my side has been a scramble since month-end, so I get why it landed badly. What day would be workable for you to have everything in?

Thanks, I appreciate that. Ideally I'd need the figures by Wednesday end of day, so we have two days to put the report together before it goes out on Friday. Would that be realistic for your side, or is there something that makes it tricky?
Wednesday end of day is doable in a good week, but month-end really is brutal on our side. Could we agree on a fixed day that works for both of us from now on?

Yeah, that makes sense, and I appreciate you being straight with me about month-end. How about we say Thursday morning as a fixed day then? That would still give us enough time before Friday, and if month-end is a nightmare, you can just give me a heads-up on the Monday so I can plan around it.
Thursday morning works for me, grand. Is there anything else you'd need from my side to get the report out on Friday?

judge.voice: Declan is genuinely good company: "grand", "a scramble since month-end", the euro-eating coffee machine. That's what a Dublin colleague sounds like, and my own diplomatic lines held up without him dumbing anything down. But I got nothing from it. No moment, no idiom pointed out, not even a nod to "to be fair" or "heads-up". The mission shut after three replies while Declan was still mid-question, so I didn't get a proper stretch. The recap is just counts, and it says two replies were "with help" when I never asked for help. For 25 EUR a Preply tutor would have told me something I didn't know. I'd try the banter and polite-no scene, since the partner is strong, but I wouldn't tell anyone yet. It's a good sparring partner and a poor teacher.
